subject: Deployment mode clarification & hosted eval next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@nuturehealth.com>, Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@nuturehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode recap + hosted eval options

Thanks again for your time today — great to meet the NutureHealth team. Quick recap from our demo and proposed next steps so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: clinical-summary generation for inbound patient messages (low-latency, high consistency).
- Peak pattern: 500–1,000 user-triggered requests/day; spikes during business hours (~30 reqs/min sustained, occasional bursts to 120 reqs/min).
- Data residency: production data must remain in US; evaluation data can be synthetic.
- Security: SOC 2 + audit log visibility required for procurement committee.

Hosted evaluation recommendation
- Start with a short hosted evaluation (2 dedicated endpoints) so you can validate latency and output quality without a commitment. Hosted gives: fast onboarding, adjustable rate-limits, prefix caching, and transparent token billing.
- If you need predictable throughput and guaranteed capacity, we can map that to Dedicated per-month reserved pools. For fully isolated networking (VPC/on-prem), we’d move to Private.

Questions for you
1) Can you confirm the sustained burst profile (typical minutes of 120 reqs/min?)
2) Any specific SLA or RTO/RPO expectations for this evaluation?
3) Who on procurement will own SOC2 artifact review?

Attachments: RWI-hosted-quickstart.pdf (quickstart + endpoints + sample rate-limit configs), Mutual-Action-Plan-NutureHealth-v1.xlsx (draft timeline & owners).

Proposed immediate next steps
- Spin up hosted evaluation endpoints (2) this week with a 2-week test window.
- Technical deep-dive with Rishi for rate-limit and throughput tuning (30–45 min).
- Procurement route: share SOC2 + compliance package.

I can provision the hosted endpoints at the default rate-limits and bump them after we validate. If you prefer we can price a short Dedicated pilot instead — I’m happy to walk through numbers.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Vanessa — thanks for the detailed recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Spike profile: the 120 reqs/min is an upper-bound short burst (2–5 minutes) during shift changes, sustained peaks are closer to 30–40 reqs/min.
- Data residency: production must be deployed in the US (east coast), eval can run in US-west.
- Procurement will own SOC2 review (I loop in procurement lead once we have the artifacts).

Two questions that will determine if Hosted is viable for procurement:
1) Can hosted endpoints be restricted to specific regions (US-east) for production?
2) What are your default rate-limits for hosted endpoints and how quickly can you raise them?

Also, can you confirm whether audit logs include token-level usage and request/response latency details? Those are explicit asks.

If Hosted meets these answers, we prefer to start there (faster) and evaluate Dedicated only if we need guaranteed throughput or VPC isolation.

—Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Product, NutureHealth

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode recap + hosted eval options (tech details)

Looping in a few quick technical answers you can forward to Sarah/Tom. Short answers here — happy to join a deep-dive.

1) Region scoping: Hosted API supports region pinning for deployments. For production we can pin endpoints to us-east-1 (we run regional control plane + routing). Eval in us-west is fine.

2) Rate-limits & bursting: Default hosted per-tenant limits are conservative (100 requests/min per endpoint). We can increase limits for an evaluation to meet your burst profile (120 reqs/min) within 24 hours. For sustained higher throughput we recommend either: increase endpoint concurrency on hosted or provision a small Dedicated pool (reserved vGPU capacity) for predictable SLA-backed throughput.

3) Observability / audit logs: Yes — audit logs include token-level counts, per-request latency, and trace ids. We can provide a sample log and a short playbook for ingestion into your observability stack.

4) SOC 2 / compliance docs: I attached a link to our SOC2 package (internal doc) and the compliance checklist. Procurement will get the full package via our secure share.

Suggested hosted eval config
- 2 endpoints: primary (us-east-1) and staging (us-west-2)
- Eval rate-limits: primary 200 reqs/min (temporary for pilot), staging 100 reqs/min
- KV/prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts to reduce token usage

If they expect consistent 5000–10,000 reqs/day with spikes multi-hour, we should recommend Dedicated. For now, hosted looks like the fastest path.

—Rishi
